property_summary: If withdrawAll is called by a non-owner, the call always reverts (i.e., only the owner can successfully call withdrawAll).
If the provided caller address is not equal to c.owner(), then calling c.withdrawAll(caller) must revert.
If the provided caller address is not the contract's owner, the call reverts.
If the provided caller is not the contract's owner, then calling withdrawAll with that caller should revert (i.e., (caller != c.owner()) == reverted).

For any caller and any recipient, the reference contract always forwards its entire balance when withdrawAll is called by the owner (including when recipient is address(0)), but the mutant rejects calls with recipient == address(0) causing withdrawAll to revert for that input.

For any recipient address and any contract balance, when called by owner withdrawAll always succeeds (does not revert) in the reference C; the mutant adds a require that reverts when recipient == address(0), so there exist inputs (recipient == address(0)) where the mutant reverts but the reference does not.

For any non-zero recipient address and any contract balance, when the owner calls withdrawAll(recipient) the call succeeds and forwards the contract balance; the mutant adds a require disallowing address(0) causing a revert when recipient == address(0) (so we restrict to non-zero recipient to make the property hold for the reference and fail on the mutant only for zero address).

For any recipient address that is NOT the zero address, when the owner calls withdrawAll(recipient) the call succeeds and the contract's balance becomes 0; the mutant adds a require disallowing the zero address but still must allow non-zero recipients — we assert the reference always succeeds and clears balance for any non-zero recipient while the mutant will revert for recipient == address(0) (so by fuzzing recipients including zero we find a difference).

For any recipient address, when the owner calls withdrawAll(recipient) the reference C always forwards its entire balance (succeeds) and sets its balance to 0; the mutant adds a require disallowing address(0) so it can revert when recipient == address(0), breaking the universal success property.
After withdrawAll is called by the owner, the provided _recipient address receives the contract's balance (so address(c).balance becomes 0 and address(_recipient) increases by that amount).
If withdrawAll(...) reverts then the caller is not the owner (i.e., non-owners cannot successfully call withdrawAll).

If withdrawAll(...) does not revert then the contract's balance becomes zero and the recipient argument receives those funds (so the caller can cause the contract to empty into the provided recipient).
If withdrawAll succeeds when called by the owner, the specified _recipient must receive the contract's balance (i.e., the caller can direct funds to any arbitrary recipient address).
Only the contract owner can successfully call withdrawAll; any call by a non-owner must revert.

For any caller who is the owner and any recipient address, after calling withdrawAll(recipient) the entire contract balance is forwarded to the provided recipient; the mutant instead always sends the balance to owner, breaking this when recipient != owner and balance>0.
After withdrawAll by the owner, the contract's balance becomes zero (all funds are forwarded to the recipient).
If the caller is the owner then withdrawAll should not revert (i.e., call completes successfully).
Only the owner can cause withdrawAll to succeed: if msg.sender equals c.owner(), then withdrawAll must not revert and thus reverted == false.
If the contract C has a positive balance and the caller is the owner, then after calling withdrawAll the balance of C becomes zero and the call does not revert.
